To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
previous exposure to antipseudomonas antibiotic therapy is associated with subsequent resistance to the antibiotic used.
exposure to an antipsuedomonal antibiotic as monotherapy is associated with subsequent resistance to itself.
exposure to antipseudomonad antibiotics is associated with subsequent resistance of Pseudomonasaeruginosa to the same antibiotic, especially if it was used as monotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of the previous use of antibiotics on the susceptibility pattern and resistance of P. aerugosa strains isolated from bacteremic patients.
the development of a new method of measuring the susceptibility of P. aeroginosa bacteremic isolats to antipseudomonas antibiotic.
the influence of previous exposure to antibiotics on the susceptibility pattern and the outcome of Pseudomonasaeruginosa bacteremia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exposure to any antipsudomonal antibiotic is associated with a significant increase in resistance to that same drug.
previous exposure to antipseudomonas antibiotics increases the risk for subsequent resistance to the same antibiotic.
previous exposure to an antipsuedomonal antibiotic, especially as a monotherapy, is associated with an increased resistance of P. aerugionosa bacteremic isolats to the same antibiotic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with a previous exposure to antibiotics are at a higher risk of developing resistance when they are exposed to these antibiotics again.
the risk of developing resistance to ceftizidime and impienem is significantly increased in patients previously exposed to these agents.
patients who had been previously exposed to antibiotic therapy for Pseudomonas infection were more likely to be resistant to the antibiotics used in that therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clinicians should avoid read-ministering previously prescribed antipseudomnal antibiotics when initiating empirictreatments for possible P. Aeruginosa
patients who are treated for Pseudomonas infection with an antibiotic should not be re-treated with that same antibiotic.
the risk of resistance to a specific antipseudomnal agent is increased if a patient has been previously exposed to that same agent.
